title: Development of Rainfall Intensity-Duration-Frequency Curve for Ulhas River Basin in Thane District, India
content: Ulhas River Basin is situated in the western part of India, within Thane district of Maharashtra state. The Ulhas River floods frequently almost every year which results in heavy economic and tragic human life losses. The urban expansion of Ulhas River Basin has intensified flood vulnerability as existing urban drainage systems exceed their design capacity since it is not evaluated accurately. Hydraulic designers are adopting non-site-specific IDF relationships due to unavailability of IDF (Intensity-Duration-Frequency) curves suitable for Ulhas River Basin. The daily rainfall data were collected for seven meteorological rainfall gauge stations located inside Ulhas River Basin from the year 1998 to 2025. For each rainfall gauge station, the rainfall data were analyzed to extract the daily maximum rainfall for each year which was subsequently used in frequency distribution analysis and best fitting probability distribution was chosen using AIC (Akaike Information Criterion) and BIC (Bayesian Information Criterion) goodness of fit tests. The frequency analysis shows that the daily maximum rainfall data fits well for both Gumbel Extreme Value distribution (GEV) and Gumbel distribution. Subsequently Gumbel distribution was applied to estimate the maximum rainfall depth corresponding to return periods such as 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 and 500 years. The imperial rainfall reduction formula provided by IMD (Indian Meteorological Department) was utilized to estimate the respective rainfall depth for shorter duration of rainfall such as 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 180, 360, 720 and 1440 minutes. Finally, IDF curves were prepared for all seven cities inside Ulhas river Basin. The IDF results demonstrated that all seven IDF curves show similar pattern with marginal differences in rainfall intensities. The IDF curves parameters C, m and e were estimate by transforming the standard IDF equation into logarithmic form for each city and their accuracy was assessed through RMSE (Root mean square) and R2 values and results were further enhanced by minimizing the error. The IDF curve equation is developed for cities Thane, Ulhas Nagar, Ambernath, Bhiwandi, Murbad, Shahpur, Kalyna & Ulhas river Basin which provide valuable directions to urban planners and hydraulic engineers in sizing the urban stormwater drainage system. The developed IDF curves and equations provides a reliable tool to engineers which will help them in infrastructure planning, urban flood management, and hydraulic designs storm water drainage structures.
